slides.text: I am horribly face-blind, which is exactly how I ended up giving a tearful, ten-minute eulogy at the wrong funeral. I thought I was burying my great-uncle Arthur, a man who loved fishing and tax evasion. I stood at the podium, sobbing uncontrollably, talking about how 'Arthur' once physically fought a rabid raccoon for a hotdog. The crowd was completely silent. Stunned. Mesmerized by my public grief.

'Arthur was a rebel,' I cried, slamming my fist passionately on the wooden podium. 'He didn't care about the IRS, and he didn't care about pants!' An elderly woman in the front row instantly fainted. A man in a very expensive suit slowly raised his hand. 'Excuse me,' he whispered, looking utterly terrified. 'This is the funeral for Margaret, the former President of the National Gardening Association.'

I froze. I slowly looked at the open casket. It was definitely an elderly woman in a floral dress. I couldn't just walk away; I was in way too deep. I leaned back into the microphone. 'And Margaret,' I declared, pointing fiercely at the casket, 'also fought that raccoon! They were a tag team! A gardening, hotdog-loving duo!' The crowd erupted into wild applause. I was invited to the wake.
